summary: The root ثوي primarily means to reside, dwell, or remain in a place. It implies settling down and taking up abode, often for an extended period.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: ثَوَى ثوى ثوة ثوي (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) بِالمَكَانِ, (S, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) and فِيهِ, (Msb,) and ثَوَى المَكَانَ, (S, * M, Msb, K,) aor. ثَوِىَ, (T, S, Msb, K,) inf. n. ثَوَآءُ (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K) and ثُوِىٌّ (S, M, Mgh, K) and مَثْوًى; (T, M;) and (T, S, M, Msb, K) بالمكان, (S, M, K,) or فيه; (so in the CK;) He remained, stayed, dwelt, or abode, (T, S, Mgh, Msb,) in the place: (S, Mgh, Msb:) or he remained, stayed, dwelt, or abode, long (Lth, T, M, K) therein: (M, K:) or he alighted, or…

اثوى أثوى أثوي اثوى اثوي ثوى ثوي: see 1. اثواهُ He made him to remain, stay, dwell, or abide; (S, Msb, K;) or to remain, &c., long; (M, K;) in a place; (M, K;) and, (Kr, S, M, K,) inf. n. تَثْوِيَةٌ, (S,) signifies the same. (Kr, S, M, K.) [In the CK, ثَوَيْتُهُ is erroneously put for ثَوَّيْتُهُ.] And He lodged him; made him his guest; or entertained him as a guest. (M, K.) You say, أَنْزَلَنِى فَأَثْوَانِى ثَوَآءً حَسَنًا [ He lodged me, and entertained me well as a guest ]. (T.)
تثوّاهُ تثواه تثواة He became his guest. (TA.)
ثَآءٌ ثآء [mentioned in this art. in the K, as “ A certain letter of the alphabet, ” namely, ث ]: see art. ثوأ: ISd holds its ا to be originally و. (TA.)
ثَاىٌ ثاى ثاي: see what next follows.
ثَاوَةٌ ثاوه ثاوة: see what next follows.

ثَايَةٌ ثايه ثاية, (S, M, K,) without ء, (S,) formed by permutation from ثوية, though the author of the Kitáb [i. e. Sb] holds the ا to be originally ى, (M,) The lodging-place, or nightly resting-place, of camels, (ISk, S, M, K,) and of sheep or goats, (ISk, S,) when they have gone away to a distance in the pasture, or around the tents or houses; (ISk, S, M, K;) as also and: (K:) or the first and second, (AZ, T, S, M,) and the third also, (M,) signify the lodging-place, or nightly…
ثُوَّةٌ ثوه ثوة: see art. ثو: and see ثَايَةٌ in the present art., above.

ثَوِىٌّ ثوى ثوة ثوي A guest: (IAar, T, S, M, K:) the vulgar erroneously pronounce it تِوِىٌّ. (TA. [See also مَثْوًى.]) Remaining, staying, dwelling, or abiding; as also تَوِىٌّ; but the former is better known in this sense. (M in art. توى.) One who abides ( مُجَاوِرٌ [generally meaning for the purpose of study ]) in either of the two sacred cities or territories [ of Mekkeh and El-Medeeneh ].
ثُوِىٌّ ثوى ثوة ثوي: see art. ثو. Also an inf. n. of 1. (S &c.)
ثَوِيَّةٌ ثوي ثويه ثوية: see ثَايَةٌ, above, in two places. Also A woman (K, TA) to whom one betakes himself to remain, stay, dwell, or abide, with her ( يُثْوَى إِلَيْهَا ). (TA.)

ثَاوٍ ثاو part. n. of 1; (Msb;) [ Remaining, &c.: or remaining, &c., long: ] a stranger remaining, staying, dwelling, or abiding, in a country, or town: (T:) or ثَاوِى بَلْدَةٍ a stranger who keeps to a country, or town. (M.) A man remaining in his grave. (IB, TA.)
ثَاوِىُّ ثاوى ثاوي: see ثَائِىٌّ, in art. ثوأ. You say قَافِيَةٌ ثَاوِيَّةٌ [in the CK, erroneously, ثاوِيَةٌ ] A rhyme of which the characteristic is ث. (K, * TA.)

مَثْوًى و A place where one remains, stays, dwells, or abides; (T;) a place of alighting or abode, an abode, or a dwelling, (T, M, Mgh, Msb,) of a man: (T:) pl. مَثَاوٍ (T, M, Mgh, Msb, K.) Hence, أَبُو المَثْوَى The master (M, K) of the house or tent, (M,) or of the place where one alights or abides, or of the abode or dwelling. (K.) And أُمُّ المَثْوَى The mistress of the house or tent.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
